backlogged.summary: lib/run.mjs's hooksOff() still uses one core.hooksPath directory per process (created once via makeTempDir, reused across the run, removed at process exit) rather than per git call. It's a unique mkdtemp path (not the shared literal 'harness-no-hooks-dir' B29 described), so it isn't the same bug, and AC-2 explicitly scopes the per-call requirement to verify/eval only — but it's worth aligning with the same per-call pattern for consistency.

The base vacuity check runs with a live symlink/junction to the working tree's node_modules, so a base-side check that writes under node_modules (e.g. node_modules/.cache from babel/jest/vite) modifies the working tree's node_modules. SC-1 only covers the harness's own link handling; consider documenting this or linking read-only where possible.

In ensureOverlaidBase, newOnBase is computed with fs.lstatSync(path.join(dir, f)) after the node_modules link exists. For an overlay path under node_modules/ this resolves through the link into the working tree, so a feature-created file there is wrongly treated as present on base (affects only entry-script withholding for files under node_modules).

commandPrograms splits only on '&&', '||', ';', '|' (per contract). A newline-separated multi-line check (e.g. 'cd sub\njest') still judges only the first program, so a missing later program remains a plain exit-127 failure.

Windows junction cleanup relies on fs.lstatSync(link).isSymbolicLink() being true for junctions and on fs.rmSync/git worktree remove not descending into junctions; the SC-1/ES-1 behaviour is only exercised on POSIX in this review (tests use symlinks on macOS).
